newsitem.title: UK: Johnson Matthey H1 up, despite tough markets.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Matthey H1 up, despite tough markets.

text.p: Johnson Matthey, the British precious metals and specialist materials company, first half profits rose nine percent to 51.2 million stg despite difficult trading conditions in some markets, chairman David Davies said.
"Our substantial investment in electronic materials is making good progress and catalytic systems has recovered well," Davies said.The interim dividend was up seven percent at 4.7p.

Davies said electronic materials profits were up 15 pct despite a downturn in parts of the semiconductor industry. Catalytic systems' profits were up 22 pct and also well ahead of the second half of last year.

Results benefitted from last year's restructuring and growth in major car markets, he said. Precious metals' profits were only just ahead of last year's first half due to lower platinum group metal prices.

Davies said cash flow was positive in both catalytic systems and precious metals. Cookson Matthey Ceramics had a disappointing first half, with depressed European tile markets holding back growth, he added.
Overall sales were up only two pct over the first half of last year, while operating profits rose eight pct to 55.3 million stg. Earnings per share were up three pct at 16.9p.
